compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

This store's enrichment queue holds **898 pending entries across 4,903 tickets**
(measured 2026-08-21). `enrich_drain.drain` processes at most `overlap_drain_batch`
(default 5) SUCCESSES per run, and `overlap.queue.pending_enrichment` returns ids **sorted**,
so each run works a fixed prefix of the same sorted list. Entries late in sort order are
reached only once everything ahead of them drains.

Two consequences, both observable today:

**1. Late-sorted entries starve.** The three tickets from bug `569c-931f-69a2-4c1d` sit at
sorted indices **458 / 499 / 786**. Even with that bug fixed — their prompts now bound
correctly and they enrich in ~8 s against the real provider — they will not reach `done`
until the ~458-deep backlog ahead of them clears.

**2. The O(1) gate marker can never engage, so every store write pays a full scan.**
`pending_enrichment` clears the gate marker whenever it finds anything pending
(`queue.py:374-375`). With 898 entries permanently pending, the marker is cleared on every
probe, `958e-f4b3-275c-4154`'s fast path is unreachable on this store, and ordinary writes
log:

```
WARNING rebar.llm.enrich_drain: enrich drain gate check took ~900-1200 ms (> 20 ms budget)
```

That warning fires on essentially **100% of writes** here. It is frequently misattributed to
whichever enrichment bug is currently open; the actual dominant cause is the backlog depth.

## Open questions for whoever claims this
- Is 898 a transient backlog draining down after bug `3198-438c-72a5-470f` (detached drain
  children dying at `getcwd()`) was fixed, or is enqueue outpacing a 5-per-write drain?
  Measure the trend before changing anything.
- If it is steady-state, the batch cap and/or the sorted iteration order are the levers:
  sorted order makes starvation deterministic rather than fair. Oldest-`not_before_ns` first,
  or a rotating start offset, would at least make it uniform.
- Should the gate marker record "nothing pending BEFORE index N" rather than being all-or-
  nothing, so a deep backlog does not permanently disable the fast path?

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The backlog trend is measured and reported (draining vs steady-state vs growing).
- [ ] No queue entry can be starved indefinitely by sort position while other entries drain.
- [ ] On a store with a deep backlog, the write-path gate check is back inside its budget (or
      the budget/warning is re-justified for that regime).
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and CI's pytest invocation are green.

## Provenance
Found while debugging `569c-931f-69a2-4c1d`. It was tested and REJECTED as that bug's root
cause — the three entries were observed being claimed and failing the provider 400 on demand,
which starvation alone cannot explain — but it is a real independent problem, and it is the
reason that bug's AC3 ("the three entries reach `done` on this store") is not satisfied by
that bug's fix alone.
compiled_state.title: deep enrichment backlog starves late entries
